channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Lula encontra empresários em evento em São Paulo após proibir bets
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva met with over 500 business leaders in São Paulo, following the ban on betting, at an event that gathered leaders from various economic sectors. The meeting emphasized dialogue between government and business, focusing on economic issues and development. The presence of prominent figures reinforced the importance of discussing public policies and growth.

item.title: Governo precisará compensar perda de R$ 6,8 bi em receitas com bets até 2027, diz ministro
item.description: The federal government will need to offset a loss of R$ 6.8 billion in revenue from online betting until 2027, following the ban on the activity. According to Minister Bruno Moretti, the 2027 budget draft will see adjustments to redirect R$ 5 billion to the Desenrola 3.0 program and seek new revenue sources.

item.title: Governo vai usar IA e canal de denúncia para derrubar sites de apostas
item.description: The Lula government announced the use of artificial intelligence and a complaint channel to identify and combat illegal betting sites in Brazil. The measure is part of an offensive against unregulated betting in the country.

item.title: Entenda como vai funciona o novo Desenrola, que prevê desconto de até 90% nas dívidas
item.description: The Lula government launched the third phase of Desenrola Brasil, a program offering up to 90% discounts for indebted individuals, with changes from previous versions. The announcement took place in São Paulo, just before the 2026 presidential elections.

item.title: Mendonça derruba posts de Erika Hilton e Leonardo Boff sobre Nossa Senhora
item.description: TSE vice-president Minister André Mendonça removed a post by actor Antonio Tabet at the request of Flávio Bolsonaro, escalating a series of posts related to Our Lady. The action was criticized for allegedly censoring religious statements in the electoral context.

item.title: Leia a íntegra da medida provisória que acaba com as bets no Brasil
item.description: President Lula published a provisional measure banning online betting houses, known as 'bets', with immediate effect. The measure aims to combat family debt and gambling addiction, but must be approved by Congress within 120 days. Lula justified the decision by comparing gambling addiction to crack and emphasized the need for a drastic solution.

item.title: Funcionário do Planalto estimula fake news sobre Nossa Senhora
item.description: George Marques, the coordinator of Strategy and Information at the Presidency's Secretariat of Communication, shared a false news story claiming that the PL and Flávio Bolsonaro were behind a project to strip Nossa Senhora Aparecida of her title as patron saint of Brazil. The post was removed after a court order from Minister André Mendonça of the TSE. Marques denied agreeing with the content, saying the sharing was unintentional.

item.title: Confira como foi a sexta-feira (25) dos presidenciáveis
item.description: On Friday (25), presidential candidates carried out campaigns across the country with walks, parades, and events with supporters. Lula advocated for banning sports betting sites, while Caiado emphasized debt renegotiation and subsidies for agribusiness. Candidates also addressed topics such as education, security, and the environment during their rallies and interviews.

item.title: STF condena Eduardo Bolsonaro por difamação contra Tabata Amaral
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court convicted former congressman Eduardo Bolsonaro for defamation against lawmaker Tabata Amaral, imposing a one-year prison sentence and $80,000 in fines. The case involved social media posts about Tabata's bill regarding feminine hygiene products. Justice Alexandre de Moraes served as the rapporteur.

item.title: Fake news da padroeira pode virar tiro no pé para Lula com católicos
item.description: A fake news about Nossa Senhora Aparecida sparked controversy between Catholics and evangelicals on social media, potentially hurting Lula by losing Catholic Church support. Analysts discuss the strategy's impact, Alckmin's stance, and the 2026 religious vote competition.

item.title: O encontro de Lula e Joesley Batista
item.description: President Lula attended a dinner with business leaders in São Paulo, including Joesley Batista and Rubens Ometto, following the announcement of a ban on bets in the country. The event gathered figures from the productive sector and government allies such as Geraldo Alckmin and Fernando Haddad.

item.title: Lula compara vício em bets a crack e câncer para justificar proibição
item.description: President Lula compared online betting addiction to crack and cancer to justify banning bets through a provisional decree. The measure also criminalizes those who operate or advertise betting platforms.

item.title: Governo Lula fará força-tarefa para combater mercado ilegal de bets
item.description: The Lula government established a task force to combat the illegal online betting market, including a total ban on sports betting, website and bank account blocking, and asset seizure for public security. The provisional measure takes effect immediately and requires congressional approval within 120 days, enjoying strong public support among women and evangelicals ahead of the October 2026 election.

item.title: Tabet ironiza repercussão de post sobre Flávio: "Perdão, família miliciana"
item.description: Antonio Tabet posted an ironic criticism of Flávio Bolsonaro's family, accusing them of attacking Our Lady of Aparecida, which sparked widespread backlash. Following the reaction, TSE Minister André Mendonça ordered the removal of the post, deeming the accusation unfounded. Tabet later mocked the situation by asking for 'forgiveness' from the 'military family' amid the controversy.

item.title: Datafolha: como está a disputa entre Lula e Flávio em SP, MG, RJ, DF e PE
item.description: The latest Datafolha poll shows a technical tie between Lula and Flávio in Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, and the Federal District, while Flávio leads in São Paulo and Lula holds an advantage in Pernambuco. Nationally, both candidates remain tied with 40% and 36% of first-round voting intentions. The surveys were conducted between September 22 and 24, with a margin of error of 3 percentage points.

item.title: Quem pode tirar o título de padroeira do Brasil? Não é o presidente
item.description: The rumor that Flávio Bolsonaro proposed removing Our Lady of Aparecida as Brazil's patron saint went viral after the first round of elections. This false claim has circulated since 2018 without any factual basis. The Brazilian presidency has no authority to change the country's patron saint, as such a designation depends on a papal decree, not domestic political power.

item.title: Associação das bets diz que proibição pegou setor de surpresa
item.description: The National Association of Games and Lotteries (ANJL) criticized the provisional decree signed by Lula banning 'betting shops' in Brazil, calling it a political rather than technical decision, and announced plans for legal action, citing losses to investments and state revenue.

item.title: Apostas: governo publica MP que proíbe as bets no Brasil
item.description: The federal government published a provisional decree fully banning online betting houses in Brazil, including sports and virtual game bets. Additionally, the Desenrola 3.0 program was created to reduce family debts by purchasing financial institutions' debts with a minimum 90% discount and passing the benefit to debtors. The measure also extinguishes state and district concessions for fixed-bet lotteries.

item.title: Haddad diz que Lula “formou juízo” sobre bets
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT) supported President Lula's announcement to ban online betting ('bets') in Brazil, stating the timing is appropriate. Haddad described the situation as a 'pandemic' affecting both the economy and public health. The announcement occurred during a business event in São Paulo.

item.title: Flávio tenta responsabilizar Lula por expansão das bets, enquanto outros rivais evitam comentar veto do governo
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro criticized the MP banning sports betting and online gambling, attempting to link regulation to the Lula government using the 'father of Tigrinho' slogan. Other candidates like Augusto Cury and Ronaldo Caiado avoided direct stances, with Cury advocating for ending bets and Caiado criticizing partial solutions.

item.title: MP do fim das bets precisa ser votada em até 120 dias e tema deve ser alvo de discussão depois das eleições
item.description: President Lula signed a provisional decree banning betting apps in Brazil, suspending new deposits and blocking sites by October. The decree has a four-month validity and must be approved by Congress after elections, with a bill to criminalize the activity also planned.

item.title: Lula aciona TSE após ser chamado por Flávio de “pai do Tigrinho”
item.description: Lula's campaign filed a lawsuit with the TSE against Flávio Bolsonaro, who called him 'father of the Tigrinho' in criticism of online betting. The coalition alleges misinformation and seeks fines and suspension of the ads. Lula signed an MP banning online betting.

item.title: André Mendonça multa campanha de Lula por impulsionar vídeo contra Flávio
item.description: Minister André Mendonça fined Lula's campaign R$15,000 for boosting a video against Flávio Bolsonaro, deeming it paid amplification of negative campaigning and barring further distribution of the content.

item.title: Globo, Band e ESPN suspendem anúncios de bets no país
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) banned online betting operations in Brazil, leading to the suspension of advertising contracts with broadcasters such as Globo, ESPN, and Band. Brands like Betano, Novibet, Superbet, and Esportes da Sorte have canceled their ads.

item.title: Além das bets, jogos como o "Jogo do Tigrinho" estão proibidos no Brasil
item.description: President Lula signed a provisional decree banning online betting, including games like 'Jogo do Tigrinho', with deadlines for withdrawals and platform shutdowns. The decree will be sent to Congress and must be approved within 120 days. Lula compared the spread of betting to criminality and drug use.

item.title: Proibição das bets pode custar R$ 2,6 bilhões em disputas judiciais, alerta entidade do setor
item.description: Governor Lula bans fixed-odds betting, risking R$2.6 billion in legal compensation and losing up to R$78 billion in tax revenue between 2027 and 2030. The measure affects licensed companies and only benefits illegal sites, which dominate 40% of the market.

item.title: Novo Desenrola: governo Lula planeja R$ 15 bi para comprar dívidas dos bancos e aliviar bolso das famílias
item.description: President Lula announced Desenrola 3.0, allocating R$15bn to buy debts from banks and ease burden on heavily indebted families, focusing on debts 2 to 4.5 years overdue. The plan, alongside banning online betting platforms, aims to win votes ahead of October elections against Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Zanin manda investigar uso de IA para burlar sistema do STF
item.description: Minister Cristiano Zanin from the STF's 1st Chamber ordered an investigation into the use of artificial intelligence to circumvent the court's electronic system. The case involves a fraudulent appeal concerning racial quotas at the Minas Gerais Public Ministry, detected by the court's own AI tool.

item.title: Entenda o plano de Lula que proíbe bets e lança Desenrola 3.0
item.description: The federal government proposed a provisional measure banning new deposits on online betting platforms, requiring the removal of advertising, and recreating the Desenrola Brasil program in its 3rd phase, targeting families with overdue debts between 2 and 4.5 years, with a 90% discount on R$300 billion in debts. The debt auction is scheduled for November 2026, with funds fully repaid to debtors.

item.title: Com veto às bets, Lula muda rumo e contraria medidas da própria gestão
item.description: President Lula vetoed measures contrary to online betting, reversing the previous policy of regulating the sector. The new MP bans betting houses and criminalizes related activities, contradicting the administration that, until now, had structured and regulated the betting market.

item.title: Lula compara vício em apostas ao crack em anúncio de proibição das bets
item.description: President Lula signed a provisional decree banning online betting operations in Brazil, comparing gambling addiction to the crack epidemic. He cited cases of people in debt and criticized football clubs opposing the ban, noting that Santos and Brazil succeeded without online betting sponsorships.

item.title: Rico vira piada ao dizer que sairá do Brasil após Lula proibir bets
item.description: Rico Melquiades announced he will move to Portugal after President Lula signed a Temporary Measure banning online betting houses in Brazil. The decision was met with irony and criticism on social media. The MP takes effect on October 6th and requires congressional approval.

item.title: Cappelli afirma que candidatura do PT ao GDF favorece Celina
item.description: Cappelli argues that Leandro Grass's PT candidacy for the DF government favors Celina Leão's re-election, citing Quaest data showing Lula at 38% against 49% for Flávio Bolsonaro in a potential runoff. He questions how a PT candidate could obtain more votes than the party's own president, suggesting this would benefit Celina at the Buriti Palace. The PSB candidate calls on voters to support him as an alternative to change the course of the Federal District.

item.title: Eleição de 2026 deve ter menor número de debates de TV no 1º turno em 28 anos
item.description: The 2026 presidential election is expected to have the lowest number of televised debates in the first round since 1998, with only Band, in partnership with Estadão, having conducted debates among candidates for the Presidency. The reduction in public debate may affect transparency and the depth of electoral proposals.

item.title: Governo Lula anuncia proibição das bets no Brasil e propõe prisão para operadores
item.description: The Lula government announced the banning of sports betting and online casino games in Brazil, as part of a new economic package focused on fighting over-indebtedness and social protection. The measure aims to reduce financial losses for the population and strengthen public policies.

item.title: André Mendonça vota para absolver Eduardo Bolsonaro por acusação de difamação contra Tabata
item.description: Minister André Mendonça voted to acquit Eduardo Bolsonaro on a defamation charge against Tabata Amaral, arguing his statements are protected by parliamentary immunity. However, the majority voted to convict with a one-year prison sentence, though implementation remains undefined. The trial is taking place in the STF's virtual plenary and concludes on Friday.

item.title: Bets cogitam ir à Justiça e cobrar até dano moral de Lula: 'Setor não vai acabar amanhã'
item.description: Lula and team members consider filing a lawsuit against the legalization of online betting, citing risks to the economy and public security. The National Games and Lotteries Association claims the regulated market generates jobs and tax revenue.

item.title: Lula anuncia proibição das bets no Brasil: entenda a medida e até quando apostadores poderão sacar dinheiro
item.description: The federal government announced a provisional measure to ban online betting platforms in Brazil, known as 'bets'. Users will have until October 5th to withdraw their balances, and from October 6th onward, the platforms will be blocked. The ban was announced nine days before the first round of the 2026 elections, a time when the government seeks to improve its standing in voter intention polls.

item.title: Em agenda no DF, Michelle pede pacificação: "Não vamos brigar com lulistas"
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro (PL) and Celina Leão (PP) held a campaign parade in Vila Planalto, DF, where Michelle called for calm by avoiding confrontations with Lula supporters, emphasizing a respectful tone. The Senate candidate also criticized aggressive protesters and stressed the importance of dialogue between political opponents.

item.title: 'Proibir não é proteger': associações se posicionam contra a MP de Lula que proíbe bets no Brasil
item.description: The federal government announced a ban on sports betting in Brazil through a Provisional Measure, which also criminalizes unauthorized betting operations and promotion. Industry associations criticized the measure, arguing that prohibition may drive bettors to illegal offshore sites lacking oversight or consumer protections. Instead of banning, the associations advocate for stronger regulation, deposit and time limits, stricter advertising rules, and crackdowns on unlicensed operators.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro diz que ‘Lula tenta fazer estelionato antes da eleição’ ao proibir bets no País
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro harshly criticized the Lula government over a provisional decree banning sports betting (bets) in the country, accusing him of electoral fraud and opportunism. He pointed out that it was Lula who legalized bets and is now trying to eliminate them for political gain ahead of the elections. The PL candidate also promised to ban online casinos and platforms like Tigrinho.

item.title: José Sarney continua internado em hospital em SP e tem previsão de alta para a próxima semana
item.description: Former President José Sarney, 96, remains hospitalized at Sírio-Libanês Hospital in São Paulo, with expected discharge next week following pneumonia treatment. His daughter Roseana Sarney is running for the Federal Senate by MDB-MA.

item.title: Estudo do NetLab indica que Kwai descumpre regras do TSE sobre anúncios eleitorais
item.description: A NetLab study indicates that Kwai does not fully comply with TSE regulations regarding electoral ads, hindering the oversight of paid advertisements. The platform fails to accurately report spending, does not provide the profile of the reached audience, and limits data collection. NetLab plans to submit the report to TSE, which is already reviewing the content.

item.title: Mendonça mandar derrubar posts sobre falso apoio de Flávio a tirar ‘padroeira’ de N. S. Aparecida
item.description: Minister André Mendonça of the STF ordered the removal of 1,125 social media posts that falsely linked Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to a bill seeking to strip Nossa Senhora Aparecida of her status as Brazil’s patron saint. Left-wing profiles spread the claim that evangelicals supported removing the Catholic saint as national patroness, triggering 2.3 million interactions across major digital platforms in under 18 hours.

item.title: A aposta da campanha de Lula com a proibição das bets na reta final do primeiro turno
item.description: Lula announced the ban on sports betting and online casinos via provisional decree, linking the issue to household debt and gambling addiction. The campaign assesses that the anti-bets offensive has broad support, especially in the final stretch of the first round, aiming to consolidate this stance as a political differentiator.

item.title: Governo proíbe apostas e publicidade de bets no país, e plataformas sairão do ar
item.description: The federal government announced a complete ban on online betting in Brazil, immediately blocking new bets, deposits, and advertising, with full shutdown of websites and apps on October 6th. Users have until October 5th to withdraw balances, after the first round of elections. The measure, issued as a provisional decree, must be approved by Congress within 120 days to remain in effect.

item.title: Bets têm até o dia 5/10 para devolver dinheiro de apostadores
item.description: President Lula signed a provisional measure prohibiting online betting in Brazil, requiring platforms to return funds to bettors by October 5, with website blocking starting October 6. The measure also establishes specific crimes for the sector, bans betting advertisements, and creates a debt renegotiation program for those indebted due to gambling addiction.

item.title: Quaest em AL: Lula, 44%; Flávio Bolsonaro, 32%
item.description: A Quaest survey released on September 25, 2026 shows Lula leading the presidential race in Alagoas with 44%, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro at 32% in the projected first-round results. The poll interviewed 804 people between September 21 and 24, with a margin of error of 3 percentage points.

item.title: Datafolha em PE: Lula, 60%; Flávio Bolsonaro, 24%; Cury, 3%; Renan, 2%; Caiado, 2%
item.description: The Datafolha poll in Pernambuco shows Lula leading with 60%, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro at 24%. The runoff simulation indicates a Lula victory over Flávio, while the government's approval rating stands at 64%.

item.title: Governo federal arrecadou R$ 15,3 bilhões com bets desde o início de 2025
item.description: The federal government collected R$ 15.3 billion from betting company taxation since early 2025, helping meet fiscal targets. This week, a ban on online betting and virtual games was announced, with the tax rate expected to reach 18% by 2028.
